English

[edit]
English Wikipedia has an article on:
clef
Wikipedia

Alternative forms

[edit]
  • cleff, cliff (both obsolete)

Etymology

[edit]

Borrowed from Middle French clef, from Latin clāvis (“a key”). Doublet of clave and clavis.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /klɛf/
  • Audio (US):(file)
  • Rhymes: -ɛf

Noun

[edit]

clef (plural clefs)

  2. (music) A symbol found on a musical staff that indicates the pitches represented by the lines and the spaces on the staff [from 16th c.]

Derived terms

[edit]
  • alto clef
  • baritone clef
  • bass clef
  • C clef (C-clef)
  • cleffer
  • cleflike
  • F clef
  • G clef (G-clef)
  • neutral clef
  • octave clef
  • tenor clef
  • treble clef
  • viola clef

French

[edit]
French Wikipedia has an article on:
clef
Wikipedia fr

Alternative forms

[edit]
  • clé (more common)
  • cleph (humorous)

Etymology

[edit]

Inherited from Middle French clef, from Old French clef, from Latin clāvis, from Proto-Italic *klāwis, from Proto-Indo-European *(s)kleh₂w-. According to Bescherelle.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /kle/
  • Audio:(file)
  • Rhymes: -e
  • Homophones: clé, clefs, clés

Noun

[edit]

clef f (plural clefs)

  1. alternative spelling of clé (“key”)
  2. (music) clef
  3. (heraldry) key; the device as shown on a coat of arms

Derived terms

[edit]
  • clef de bras
  • clef de fa
  • clef de sol
  • clef d'ut
  • fermer à clef
  • mettre la clef sous la porte
  • prendre la clef des champs

Further reading

[edit]
  • “clef”, in Trésor de la langue française informatisé [Digitized Treasury of the French Language], 2012

Middle French

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Inherited from Old French clef.

Noun

[edit]

clef f (plural clefs)

  1. key

Adjective

[edit]

clef m or f (invariable)

  1. key (vitally important)

Descendants

[edit]
  • French: clef, clé
  • → English: clef

Old French

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Inherited from Latin clāvem.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ˈklɛf/

Noun

[edit]

clef oblique singular, f (oblique plural cles, nominative singular clef, nominative plural cles)

  1. key

Descendants

[edit]
  • Angevin: quié, quief
  • Bourguignon: quié
  • Champenois: quié
  • French: clé, clef (less common), cleph (humorous)
  • Gallo: tié
  • Middle French: clef
    • French: clef, clé
    • → English: clef
  • Norman: clef, clié, cllé
  • Poitevin-Saintongeais: cllai
  • Walloon: clé
